correctness.rationale: For n>=4 unit-edge rooted full-binary trees, deletion of 2 leaves loses pendant edges plus at most one cherry edge; deletion of 3 adds at most one cherry and one nested pitchfork edge. Their indicators imply VarY2=c/N2(1-c/N2), VarY3=(c(n-2)+3t)/N3-((c(n-2)+t)/N3)^2. Strict monotonicity in feasible c,t recovers shape indices, while 6m-leaf constructions have (c,t)=(2m+1,0) and (2m,2m) and strict reversal. Independently enumerated the 4-leaf direct variance pairs (2/9,0) versus (5/36,11/16). Large-size proof is the clade construction, not finite tests.
residual_risks: Rooted full-binary unit-length trees, uniform deletion without replacement of exactly 2/3 leaves; no empirical conservation ranking or topological identification from the pair.

evidence: Published 16-leaf classification uses the entire rarefaction mean+variance profile across all sample sizes, not just two variance values.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The stronger data distinguish full topologies through 15 leaves, but do not imply recovery or ranking reversal from just VarY2,VarY3 alone.

The particular inverse recovery of cherry and pitchfork counts from ONLY two near-complete variance statistics and a strict ranking-reversal family at every n=6m are not stated in the full source read or matched published Resultary classifications. Historical independent rediscovery is still possible.
residual_risks: Other phylogenetic cherry/pitchfork statistic literature could contain the precise two-stage inversion or a 6m reversal family.
